title: Email: Fw: Right Idea but Wrong Examples

content.subject: Fw: Right Idea but Wrong Examples

content.text:
Anthony Fenech
Tigers beat writer
Detroit Free Press
(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: kurt ralston <kralston2@gmail.com>
Sent: Monday, December 7, 2015 11:28 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: Right Idea but Wrong Examples 
 
Mr. Ilitch said he would spend money, but he 
won't.  The new arena district is absorbing all
the extra funds.

You wrote that he should sign Price or Sherzer.
The right examples are the signings of Pelfry, Lowe, and Saltalamacia - lower priced options
that fit the current business model of a few, well
paid stars and a roster filled in with lower cost
players.

Does the signing of Saltalamacia make Holiday
a part of a package to get a relief pitcher?  It is
amazing how much in demand defensive
catchers are.

Fans might like to read about your first year as
a beat writer.  Players, coaches, ballparks,
press boxes, cities, restaurants, plane trips ...

Who was the easiest/hardest to interview?
Was there anything unusual, any surprises,
any special places/events?  Take us through 
a typical day on the road.  What were the 
hilites and lowlights?  Any physical or mental
fatigue occur during the nine months?

The Freep took its readers on a freighter ride  
on the Great Lakes. How about taking baseball
fans on a road trip?

Congratulations on year one.  I look forward to
year number two.
